newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola's UNITA invited into diamond joint ventures.
newsitem.headline: Angola's UNITA invited into diamond joint ventures.

text.p: Foreign diamond companies operating in Angola said they had invited Angola's former rebel UNITA to join partnerships in the country's diamond areas.
In the diamond-rich Cuango valley, controlled mostly by the former rebels, companies are proposing to sell shares to UNITA to bring it legally into concessions, a company official said.

Talks with UNITA have already begun on one Cuango diamond project known as Sociadade de Desenvolvimento Mineiro (SDM), including Brazil's Odebrecht, Australia's Ashton Mining Ltd and the state diamond company Endiama.

"UNITA is taking diamonds out of our concession, but it is not hurting it much. We plan to make a huge capital investment there, something like $120 million. It is very complicated and very costly," said Otacilio Carvalho, Odebretch's director of operations for southern Africa .
"We even plan to divert the Cuango to mine the river bed, I doubt UNITA has the resources to do that."
Carvalho says Endiama officials representing SDM have already talked to UNITA about joining the venture.
"They have talked to them about it and the government has given the go ahead to the joint venture to speak to UNITA about working out an arrangement.
"The feeling is we will work out some sort of sale of current shares of SDM to UNITA. The number I have heard is something like selling them a 10 percent share," Carvalho said.
But a senior UNITA official in Luanda dismissed the idea.
"I have not seen Endiama buying any shares," he said. "Just as Endiama does not have to buy shares UNITA will not buy shares. We expect our rights to those diamond areas to be recognised."
U.S. diamond dealer Maurice Templesman of Lazar Kaplan recently travelled to UNITA's central stronghold in Bailundo for talks with leader Jonas Savimbi on diamonds.
During Templesman's frequent visits to Angola he is also often the guest of President Jose Eduardo dos Santos.
"Templesman spent some time with Dr Savimbi last week," the UNITA official said. "They talked about number of things, yes, including diamonds."
The world's diamond giant De Beers Consolidated Mines is also more optimistic about its future in Angola.

It signed an agreement with Endiama last year to search for diamonds in three areas of Angola. Just last month it announced that heads of agreement had been signed with Endiama for the construction of a diamond sorting centre in Luanda.
De Beers' special board representative for Angola, Jim McLuskie said in an interview recently the company has contact with UNITA through the government.

"We do have contact with UNITA through the government. We gave a presentation on the project and asked for cooperation but we're still waiting for a response. We've been waiting since September," he said.
Industry sources said talks between UNITA and the government over diamonds are making good progress.
"These negotiations are complex but we are seeing some progress. Some of the deals have already been agreed to and only need the approval of the Council of Ministers," an analyst said.
The analyst said about three separate negotiations were underway to end tensions over ownership of the diamond areas, which produce up to $1 billion annually.

Another analysts said an agreement had already been reached between UNITA and Endiama which will allow UNITA to continue operating in most of the areas it controls, provided that it registers with Endiama and pays taxes on production.
It is estimated that UNITA earns between $300 and $600 million a year in diamond revenue.
